title: U.S. House · Ohio's 15th District
area: Central Ohio, including Fairfield, Pickaway and part of Franklin counties.

context.text: Incumbent Mike Carey (R) advanced from the May 5, 2026 Republican primary; Samuel Ronan appeared on that primary's ballot but was disqualified, and he is now running in the general election as an independent write-in candidate. Don Leonard (D) defeated Adam Miller in the Democratic primary. Brennan Barrington won the Libertarian primary. Gary Josephson is also running as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Mike Carey is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 15th Congressional District, which he has represented since a 2021 special election. He previously worked in coal-industry government affairs, including as president of the Ohio Coal Association.

background.text: Born in Sabina, Ohio; graduated from East Clinton High School (1989) and served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1989 to 1999.
Earned an A.S. in economics from Marion Military Institute (1991) and a B.A. in history from Ohio State University (1993).
Worked as vice president of government affairs at American Consolidated Natural Resources and at Murray Energy Corporation, and as chairman and president of the Ohio Coal Association.

positions.summary: In January 2026 he said he voted to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits so constituents with those plans do not lose access.
positions.quote: I voted today to extend the enhanced tax credits for ACA plans.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security and Work and Welfare subcommittees), the House Committee on Budget, and the Committee on House Administration's Modernization and Innovation Subcommittee (119th Congress, 2025-2026).

summary.text: Don Leonard is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. He is a professor of city and regional planning at Ohio State University and a former U.S. Peace Corps volunteer.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and a master's degree in regional development from the University of Massachusetts, Lowell, and a Ph.D. in government from Cornell University.
Works as a professor of city and regional planning at The Ohio State University; served in the U.S. Peace Corps in South America.

positions.summary: His survey answer calls for giving all Americans access to a public option for health insurance and cutting out-of-pocket private insurance costs in half.
positions.quote: We must cut the out-of-pocket cost of private health insurance in half while at the same time ensuring that all Americans have access to a public option for their health insurance.

positions.summary: His survey answer lists universal childcare as a priority, including expanding Head Start and subsidies for private care.
positions.quote: UNIVERSAL CHILDCARE: Childcare should not cost families a second mortgage. Expand head start and provide subsidies for private care.

positions.summary: His survey answer says the "tariff war" threatened to drive up prices and disrupt the supply chain.
positions.quote: Trump’s tariff war was threatening to drive up prices, crash the supply chain, and wipe out everyone’s retirement savings.

candidates.name: Brennan Barrington

summary.text: Brennan Barrington is the Libertarian Party nominee for Ohio's 15th Congressional District.

background.text: Graduated from Licking Heights High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Ohio State University in 2019.

priorities.text: Lists cutting taxes, spending and regulations, and returning power from Washington to states, cities and individuals, as a key campaign message.
priorities.quote: Cut taxes, spending, and regulations: My goal is to return as much power as possible from DC to states, cities, and most of all individual citizens.

priorities.text: Lists electoral reform as a key campaign message: ranked choice voting for Senate elections, proportional representation for the House, and expanding the House to about 1,000 members.
Lists a tax shift from productive work to what he calls nonproductive extraction, including a tax on greenhouse gas emissions with a dividend paid to all citizens.

positions.summary: Platform opposes federal restrictions on manufacture and possession of weapons other than weapons of mass destruction.
positions.quote: I oppose all federal restrictions on the manufacture and possession of weapons, other than weapons of mass destruction.

positions.summary: Platform says federal funding should be conditioned on eliminating legal barriers to high-density housing construction.
positions.quote: Any federal funding should be conditioned on eliminating legal barriers to high-density housing construction and use where demand for it exists, to the full extent constitutionally permissible.

positions.summary: Platform says rent controls and subsidies do not reduce costs.
positions.quote: Subsidies and rent controls proposed by some left-wing candidates do not reduce the costs; they only shift them.

positions.summary: Platform says ending the current tariffs would help lower consumer prices.
positions.quote: Ending these is low-hanging fruit for lowering the costs of consumer goods for ordinary Americans, including fuel.

positions.summary: Platform proposes requiring a joint resolution of Congress to authorize military operations in another country.
positions.quote: I would propose a Constitutional amendment to reclaim the Congressional power over war.

statements.quote: Greenhouse gas emissions which cause harmful climate change are a textbook negative externality.
statements.context: On his campaign platform page, describing his proposed carbon tax with a citizen dividend

statements.quote: There are enormous gains to be obtained by authorizing entry for all potential immigrants willing and able to work or otherwise support themselves in our society without government assistance.

candidates.researchNotes: From his campaign platform page and Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026). Stances are set only where the platform text directly addresses the issue statement; his positions on abortion, school choice and minimum wage were not found.

candidates.name: Gary Josephson
candidates.ballotNote: Filed as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Gary Josephson is an independent write-in candidate for Ohio's 15th Congressional District in the November 2026 general election.

priorities.text: In a 2022 survey for a prior U.S. House race, listed opposing stereotyping and discrimination as a campaign message.
priorities.quote: I oppose stereotyping, cults, factions, sexism, racism, and other forms of discrimination.

priorities.text: In the same 2022 survey, listed rebuilding U.S. industry using green energy, public/private partnerships and worker participation as a policy passion.
priorities.quote: Rebuilding U.S. industry using green energy, healthy production, public/private partnerships, and worker participation.

statements.quote: Coal is the past. Wind, solar, and batteries are the future. That's where the jobs are.
statements.context: In his 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, from his previous run for this seat

candidates.researchNotes: Write-in candidate with no campaign website found; only Facebook and Instagram pages, which could not be read. He has not completed the 2026 Ballotpedia survey, so the statements shown are from his 2022 survey.

candidates.name: Samuel Ronan
candidates.ballotNote: Ran in and was disqualified from the Republican primary; running in the general election as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Samuel Ronan is an independent write-in candidate for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. He ran against incumbent Mike Carey in the Republican primary but was disqualified from that result.

priorities.text: Lists the rising cost of living and housing costs as the main issue, and holding companies accountable for price increases as his first mission in Congress.
priorities.quote: The main issue Americans face today is the rising cost of living and the prohibitive cost of housing.

priorities.text: Lists abolishing ICE and Border Patrol and reallocating their funds to public services.
priorities.quote: My goal is to abolish ICE, and BPD, reallocate their funds to public services, and prosecute all members of those agencies for their many crimes.

priorities.text: Names public ownership and expansion of infrastructure as the policy area he is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Says his goal is to abolish ICE and Border Patrol.
positions.quote: My goal is to abolish ICE, and BPD, reallocate their funds to public services, and prosecute all members of those agencies for their many crimes.

positions.summary: Campaign site proposes federally funded care with no cost to individuals for non-cosmetic care.
positions.quote: Functionally, the cost of care to an individual for any medical activity, that isn't elective cosmetic surgery, shall be $0

positions.summary: Campaign site says laws limiting access to any form of abortion are nullified.
positions.quote: any laws prohibiting, punishing, or otherwise limiting access to any form of abortion are nullified

positions.summary: Campaign site lists complete divestment from fossil fuels by 2035.
positions.quote: Complete divestment from fossil fuels by 2035

candidates.researchNotes: From his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) and campaign website issue pages. His site's police page proposes federalizing and consolidating law enforcement and halting existing funding; it was not mapped to the police-funding statement.

researchNotes: No dedicated Ballotpedia profiles or other independent public records were found for write-in candidates Gary Josephson and Samuel Ronan beyond their listing as general-election candidates, so their entries are minimal. Barrington's Ballotpedia profile contains no statement of issues or Candidate Connection survey response. Neither Carey nor Leonard has completed the 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no campaign-website issue statement was available via Ballotpedia, so their priorities and positions are omitted rather than inferred. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Carey are added separately.
